description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of reasoning steps and the Pass@1 Rate (%) for two large language models—GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet—on a task evaluated in the paper “VisuoThink: Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search.” The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Reasoning Steps,” is linear and spans from 5 to 40, with major tick marks at 5, 10, 20, and 40. The y-axis, labeled “Pass@1 Rate (%)”, is linear and ranges from 0 to 100, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 20 (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; its performance increases from 6.5% at 5 steps to 32.3% at 10 steps, then to 77.4% at 20 steps, and finally to 83.9% at 40 steps. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model is represented by a solid light purple line with ‘x’ markers; its performance rises from 19.4% at 5 steps to 38.7% at 10 steps, then to 87.1% at 20 steps, and reaches 89.2% at 40 steps. Both models show a consistent upward trend in performance as the number of reasoning steps increases, with Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all evaluated step counts.
